clue.text: Tropical shrub is small, in places turning

indicators.note: in tells us the word for small sits inside the reversed word for places
turning means the word for places is read backwards before the other piece goes in

parts.note: places, as in positions or stations, are posts
wee is Scots for small

explanation.surface: A botanist notes that a tropical shrub is small and changes direction in places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link here; 'small' is the Scots word, and 'turning' gives STSOP, which the small word splits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweetsop, or sugar apple, is a small tropical American tree or shrub grown for its fruit.

clue.text: Download new undeveloped site

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of the word before it are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: An instruction to fetch a fresh file for an empty building plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the eight letters of DOWNLOAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Land covered with trees is ground that has not been built on, an undeveloped site.

clue.text: Sort of ring for fighting

definitions.meaning: the ring given when a couple agree to marry
a battle or clash between armed forces

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a betrothal (with its ring) and a military encounter or battle.

clue.text: Dressing style of Cleopatra' s youth?

definitions.meaning: a sauce poured over a plate of greens
Cleopatra calls her youth 'my salad days', so the best (cream) of that era jokingly

explanation.surface: A question about how Cleopatra dressed when she was young.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra she speaks of 'My salad days, when I was green in judgment'; 'cream' of those days completes the joke. Salad cream is a tangy British bottled dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad cream is a bottled condiment, a mayonnaise-like sauce for vegetables, hence a dressing.

clue.text: Tax due in Aug., we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the phrase is to be heard, not read, matching a spelling of the same sound

parts.note: something due in August comes before September, pre-Sept

explanation.surface: A tax bill seemingly falling due in August.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a precept is the demand by which a local authority levies a rate, a kind of local tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A precept is an order to levy local rates, so it stands for a tax demand.

clue.text: Saint is beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter of the word for is is cut off

parts.note: is, in the sense of exists or lives

explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' drops the L from LIVES. St Ives was a Persian bishop who gave his name to the Cornish town.
explanation.definitionFit: St Ives (Ivo) was a legendary hermit bishop, venerated as a saint.

clue.text: To forgive is for clergyman

definitions.meaning: completes Pope's line 'To err is human, to forgive ...', meaning godlike
a cleric or theologian, an old noun sense

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means godlike, as in Pope's proverb, and as a noun it means a priest or theologian.

clue.text: Deliberate being party to three

definitions.meaning: done on purpose, planned
three refers to clue 3 down, a betrothal; one party to it is a fiance or fiancee

explanation.walkthrough: 'three' is a cross-reference to 3 down: a person party to that betrothal is someone's future spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Intentional means planned on purpose, and the noun names a person's fiance or fiancee.

clue.text: Change requirement before exam

definitions.meaning: an alteration or amendment
going over notes and study before a test

explanation.definitionFit: The word means an amendment and also the British term for studying for an examination.

clue.text: Oriental nomad' s objective not a day ahead

indicators.note: ahead places the word for day in front of what follows

parts.note: Mon is the abbreviation for Monday

indicators.note: not tells us the a in the clue is to be dropped from the word for objective

parts.note: an objective is a goal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark about a wandering Asian tribesman's aim.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition carries a possessive 's that works as 'has'. 'not a' trims the target to GOL, and 'ahead' means the day leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Mongols are a people of the central Asian steppes, traditionally nomadic herders.

clue.text: Tending to charge in case

definitions.meaning: inclined to blame or accuse someone
the grammatical case for the direct object of a verb

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means accusing in manner, and it names the grammatical case of a verb's object.

clue.text: Moon' s appearance said to be disconcerting

definitions.note: the clue word is a participle; the answer is the verb meaning to disconcert

indicators.note: said to be tells us the moon's appearance is to be heard, matching a word of identical sound

parts.note: a phase is how the moon looks at a given time, new, full and so on

explanation.surface: The way the moon looks is reportedly unsettling.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle someone or put them off their stride is to disconcert them.

clue.text: Venomous type, the chief constable?

definitions.meaning: a poisonous American snake
copper is slang for a police officer, and the head copper is the chief

explanation.definitionFit: It is a venomous American pit viper, and whimsically the top police officer.

clue.text: Start of arithmetic sum in exam

definitions.meaning: the opening of a sum such as ... three
the British test taken at age 11 for grammar school entry

explanation.definitionFit: The eleven-plus was a British school selection test taken at eleven, and the words begin an addition sum.

clue.text: Practical judgment in various points supporting heroin

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts one piece below the other

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin
S, E, N, S, E are several compass points

explanation.surface: Sound judgment is found in different places backing a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points are N, S, E and W, so 'various points' can spell any run of them. In a down entry the supporting piece sits underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Common sense, or shrewd down-to-earth wisdom, is practical judgment.

clue.text: Like cows, but showed revulsion there' s no quiet

indicators.note: no tells us the word for quiet is removed from the word before

parts.note: to shudder is to tremble with disgust
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone recoiled in disgust at cows, though without a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows have udders, so they are equipped with milk glands.

clue.text: Complete burn-out on old range

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of burn are put out of order

parts.note: ken is range of knowledge

explanation.surface: A fire burnt out entirely on an old cooking stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' misleads as a kitchen stove but means scope of knowledge; 'out' gives UNBR, and 'on' merely means following.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole and intact, with no break in it, means complete.

clue.text: Recover for the gripping part of a journey

definitions.text: Recover for the gripping part of a journey

parts.words: Recover for the gripping part of a journey
parts.note: a tyre is re-covered with new rubber, the part that grips the road while travelling

explanation.surface: A request for something to recover the most exciting part of a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recover' is re-cover: putting a fresh gripping surface on a tyre. 'gripping' suggests exciting, but means holding the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre given a new rubber surface is a remould, re-covered on its gripping part.

clue.text: Sort of bearing left, after coming initially out of Brittany once

indicators.note: after places the letter for left behind the rest
out of tells us the letter from coming is taken out of the old name

parts.note: Armorica is the ancient name for the region of Brittany

indicators.note: initially means just the first letter of coming is wanted

explanation.surface: A story of some kind of manner shown after leaving old Brittany.
explanation.walkthrough: Armorica is the Roman-era name of Brittany; removing the C leaves ARMORIA, and 'after' sends the left letter to the end. Bearings here are heraldic, not directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic bearings are coats of arms, described with this adjective.

clue.text: Feels sorry about English hypocritical sentiments

indicators.note: about means the word for feels sorry goes around the letter for English

parts.note: pities means feels sorry for

explanation.surface: Someone sympathises with the English over two-faced feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctimonious remarks, pious platitudes, are sentiments of affected piety.

clue.text: A few mechanical words the deciding factor

parts.note: Bottom is one of the 'rude mechanicals' in A Midsummer Night's Dream, so a few words he speaks are a line by him
a line is a few spoken words

explanation.surface: Some technical jargon turns out to be what matters most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mechanical' here means one of the craftsmen in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, Bottom the weaver, not machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: The final total on an account is the crux, the factor that decides matters.

clue.text: Row over church service

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A dispute over a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Row misleads as a quarrel but is a line of seats. Tierce (terce) is the office said at the third hour of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Terce, or tierce, is one of the canonical hours, a short daily church office.

clue.text: Not one to show pleasure about rugged feature of country churchyard

indicators.note: about tells us the word that remains is turned back to front
Not means the letter for one is dropped from the word for showing pleasure

parts.note: to smile is to show pleasure
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone declining to grin at a craggy spot in a rural graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' takes I from SMILE to give SMLE, and 'about' reverses it. Gray's Elegy in a Country Churchyard begins its graveyard scene 'Beneath those rugged elms'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gray's poem describes the trees of a village churchyard as rugged, so they are its feature.

clue.text: Exaggerated how one got out of the trenches

definitions.meaning: excessive, beyond what is reasonable

definitions.text: how one got out of the trenches
definitions.meaning: First World War soldiers climbed over the parapet to attack

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means excessive, and literally describes soldiers leaving a trench in an attack.

clue.text: Cat will find last of vermin in shed

definitions.text: Cat will find last of vermin in shed

indicators.note: in tells us the final letter goes inside the word for shed

parts.note: a hut is a shed

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of vermin is used

explanation.surface: A cat will catch the last of the rats in the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' gives N, the end of 'vermin', and 'in' sets it inside HUT; the whole clue is what a cat does to vermin.
explanation.definitionFit: Chasing prey to catch or kill it is what a cat does with vermin.

clue.text: Swollen, till seed bursts out

indicators.note: bursts out says the answer emerges from within the words around it

explanation.surface: Something swells until a seed splits open.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'swolLEN TILl'; 'bursts out' is the signal that they come from inside those words.
explanation.definitionFit: A lentil is the small edible seed of a leguminous plant, a pulse.

clue.text: For knight, surrendering castle' s a loss of one place of business

definitions.text: For knight, surrendering castle' s a loss of one
definitions.meaning: in chess, giving up a rook (castle) for a knight is losing the trade known by this name
a building where merchants or brokers trade

explanation.definitionFit: In chess it names the trade of a rook for a minor piece; it is also a trading hall or bourse.

clue.text: Weaselly, tries falsely to get in relatively close

indicators.note: to get in signals that the rearranged letters are put inside the word for weaselly

parts.note: weaselly means sly, cunning

indicators.note: falsely tells us the letters of tries are to be wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A sly character tries dishonestly to win favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weaselly' is the container, not a description of the trier; 'falsely' gives ISTER, which splits the sly word after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Close as only a female sibling would be: affectionate in the way of a family relation.
